questions.question: If ΔABC is right angled at C, CD ⊥ AB, ∠A = 55° then, ∠ACD = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a **right-angled triangle** ΔABC with an **altitude CD** drawn to the **hypotenuse AB**, the angle **∠ACD** is always **complementary** to **∠A**.

⇒ **∠ACD** = 90° − **∠A**

⇒ **∠ACD** = 90° − 55°

⇒ **∠ACD** = 35°

**∴ The correct answer is 35°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

ΔABC is **right-angled** at **C** (∠ACB = 90°).

**CD** is **perpendicular** to **AB** (CD ⊥ AB).

**∠A** = 55°.

**Formula Used:**

In any **triangle**, the sum of all **interior angles** is 180°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b39951cea3bfb0a03bb2d62c164d42c9b9c216d91999f79fc569c971275a4e0e.png] 

**Calculations:**

Consider the small triangle **ΔADC**.

⇒ In **ΔADC**, we have three angles: **∠A**, **∠ADC**, and **∠ACD**.

⇒ Since **CD ⊥ AB**, the angle **∠ADC** is 90°.

⇒ Sum of angles in **ΔADC** = 180°

⇒ **∠A** + **∠ADC** + **∠ACD** = 180°

⇒ 55° + 90° + **∠ACD** = 180°

⇒ 145° + **∠ACD** = 180°

⇒ **∠ACD** = 180° − 145°

⇒ **∠ACD** = 35°

**∴ The correct answer is 35°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Similarity in Right Triangles

When an **altitude** is drawn to the **hypotenuse** of a **right triangle**, the two smaller triangles formed are **similar** to the original triangle and to each other (**ΔACD ∼ ΔCBD ∼ ΔABC**).

Angle Relationships

In the configuration above, the angles are related as: **∠ACD = ∠B** and **∠BCD = ∠A**.

Right Triangle Complementary Angles

The two **acute angles** of any **right-angled triangle** are always **complementary**, meaning their sum is exactly 90°.</p

questions.question: Which of the following is an ester?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**CH3COOC2H5 .**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• An **ester** is an **organic molecule** in which the** carboxyl group's hydrogen** is replaced with a hydrocarbon group.
 
• Esters are made up of **carboxylic acids and alcohol**. In an ester, the hydrogen is replaced by a hydrocarbon, whereas carboxylic acid possesses the -COOH group.
 
• An ester's chemical formula is** RCO2R′,** where **R** represents the** carboxylic acid's hydrocarbon** components and **R′** represents the **alcohol.**
 
• **Ethyl acetate **(ethyl ethanoate)** CH₃COOC₂H₅,** is an ester. The hydrogen on the carboxyl group of acetic acid is replaced with an ethyl group.
 
• Ethyl propanoate, propyl methanoate, propyl ethanoate, and methyl butanoate are examples of esters. **Glycerides are glycerol** fatty acid esters.
 
• Because they can act as hydrogen-bond acceptors to generate hydrogen bonds, esters are moderately** soluble in water.**
 
• They cannot, however, act as hydrogen-bond donors and so **can not self-associate.**
 
• Esters are** less polar than alcohols,** **more polar than ethers**, and **more volatile than carboxylic acids** of comparable size.
 
• Esters usually have a** fruity scent.** Because of their volatility, they can be differentiated from one another using **gas chromatography.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Acetic acid** is an** organic compound** with the chemical formula **CH₃COOH** that is **acidic and colourless**.
 
• Apart from water and other trace ingredients, **vinegar** contains at least **4% acetic acid **by volume.
 
• The** second most basic carboxylic acid **is acetic acid (after formic acid).
 
• It's a significant **chemical reagent and industrial chemical** that's used to make cellulose acetate for **photographic film**, polyvinyl acetate for **wood glue**, and** synthetic fibres and fabrics**, among other things.
 
• **Descaling treatments** made from **diluted acetic acid** are commonly used in homes.
 
• Acetic acid is a food additive with the **code E260** that is used as an **acidity regulator** and a condiment in the food industry.
 
 
 
• **CH3CHO:**
 
 
• The organic chemical compound **acetaldehyde** (IUPAC systematic name **ethanal**) has the formula CH₃CHO and is commonly abbreviated by scientists as **MeCHO (Me = methyl).**
 
• It's a **colourless gas or liquid** that boils at about room temperature.
 
• Acetaldehyde is produced by **plants** and can be found in **coffee, bread, and ripe fruit.**
 
• Acetaldehyde is "one of the most** often discovered air pollutants** with one-in-a-million **cancer risk.**
 
 
 
• **CH3COCH3:**
 
 
• The chemical molecule **acetone,** also known as **propanone or dimethyl ketone,** has the formula (CH₃)₂CO.
 
• It is the** most basic and tiniest ketone**. It's a **colourless, extremely volatile, combustible liquid **with a distinctive **pungent odour.**

questions.question: Find the area of a triangle whose vertices are (a, b + c), (a, b - c) and (-a, c).
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **vertices** (a, b + c) and (a, b − c) share the same **x-coordinate**, forming a vertical **base**.

**Base length** = |(b + c) − (b − c)| = |b + c − b + c| = 2c.

The **height** of the triangle is the horizontal distance from the third vertex (−a, c) to the line x = a.

**Height** = |a − (−a)| = 2a.

**Area** = 1/2 × Base × Height = 1/2 × 2c × 2a = 2ac.

**∴ The correct answer is 2ac.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Vertices of the triangle are (x₁, y₁) = (a, b + c), (x₂, y₂) = (a, b − c), and (x₃, y₃) = (−a, c).

**Formula Used:** Area = 1/2 |x₁(y₂ − y₃) + x₂(y₃ − y₁) + x₃(y₁ − y₂)|

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a705acc5f754300c36559576f054fe49f0db7bd980ca88d765504d2b02fc548.png] 

⇒ Area = 1/2 |a((b − c) − c) + a(c − (b + c)) + (−a)((b + c) − (b − c))|

⇒ Area = 1/2 |a(b − 2c) + a(c − b − c) − a(b + c − b + c)|

⇒ Area = 1/2 |ab − 2ac + a(−b) − a(2c)|

⇒ Area = 1/2 |ab − 2ac − ab − 2ac|

⇒ Area = 1/2 |−4ac|

⇒ Area = 2ac

**∴ The correct answer is 2ac.**

**__Additional Information__**

Area of Triangle (Coordinate Geometry)

The area of a triangle with vertices (x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₂), and (x₃, y₃) is given by 1/2 |x₁(y₂ − y₃) + x₂(y₃ − y₁) + x₃(y₁ − y₂)|.

Condition for Collinearity

Three points are **collinear** if the area of the triangle formed by them is exactly 0.

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The **public and private sectors coexist** in a mixed economy.
 
• The** central planning authority** and the** price mechanism** both decide **what, how, and for whom** to produce.** India's economy** is a mixed economy.
 
• In a mixed economy, **major economic decisions** are made by the **central government authority** in the** public sector** while the **private sector** is allowed to free play of market forces. While market forces ensured that **individual income and growth rates** were **maximized,** the **central government **ensured that **societal welfare was maximized.**
 
• A Mixed Economy's** purpose** is to **fix the problems of both a capitalist and a socialist economy** in order to develop a unique system.
 
• It upholds the** principles of private property and resource ownership,** as well as the corresponding** freedom.**
 
• It also recognizes the** perils of unrestrained capitalism.** As a result, it argues for **government control and economic planning** in order to prevent **discrimination **against the **poorest populations.**
 
• The **'Industrial Policy Resolution'** of **1948 **and the **Indian Constitution's Directive Principles** reflected this perspective.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• A traditional economy is an **economic system** in which **traditions, customs, and beliefs** help shape the goods and services the economy produces, as well as the** rule and manner of their distribution. Countries** that use this type of economic system are often** rural and farm-based.**
 
• **Examples** of traditional economies include the Inuit people in the **United States' Alaska, Canada, and the Denmark territory of Greenland. **
 
 
 
• **Command economy:**
 
 
• A command economy is a **key aspect of a political system** in which a **central governmental authority** dictates the levels of production that are permissible and the prices that may be charged for goods and services. Most industries are publicly owned.
 
• **China, North Korea, and the former Soviet Union** are all examples of command economies.
 
 
 
• **Market economy:**
 
 
• A market economy is an** economic system where two forces,** known as **supply and demand**, direct the production of goods and services.
 
• Market economies are** not controlled by a central authority** (like a government) and are instead based on **voluntary exchange.**

The Reserve Bank's** clearance of accounts** has now become a critical role.
 
• **Controller of Credit: **Since credit money forms the most important part of the supply of money, and since the supply of money has important implications for** economic stability**, the importance of the control of credit becomes obvious. ⇒ 4,000(11/10)² – 4,000]

questions.question: Who among the following has initially drafted the 'Quit India' resolution of the Indian National congress in 1942?

__
 
• During World War II, **Mahatma Gandhi** started the** Quit India Movement,** also known as the** August Movement**, during the** Bombay session of the All India Congress Committee** on** August 8, 1942**, demanding an** end to British rule** in India.
 
• After the** failure of the Cripps Mission** to **secure Indian support** for the British war effort, Gandhi made a call to** Do or Die** in his Quit India speech delivered in Bombay on 8 August 1942 at the** Gowalia Tank Maidan.**
 
• **Yusuf Meherally, **a socialist who was also a** trade unionist,** coined the slogan** "Quit India.**" He was also the** Mayor of Mumbai.** He also came up with the catchphrase **"Simon Go Back."**
 
• The movement was **opposed** by the **Muslim League**, the **Communist Party of India,** and the **Hindu Mahasabha.**
 
• There were **strikes and demonstrations** across the country during the **first phase**. The **Aga Khan Palace in Pune **was where Mahatma Gandhi was **imprisoned.** The British also detained a number of other leaders.
 
• During the **second phase of the Quit India Movement,** many peasant uprisings took place, including the** destruction of communication systems** such as railway tracks and stations, telegraph cables and poles, as well as** attacks on government buildings **and other obvious symbols of colonial authority.
 
• In the** third and last phase **of the Quit India Movement, national governments or parallel governments were formed in** isolated enclaves like Ballia, Tamluk, and Satara.**
 
• The British administration in India mercilessly **suppressed **the Quit India movement. The majority of the movement's popular leaders were arrested.
 
• To put down the movement, the British used** lathi-charge** and other harsh methods. Officials who supported the movement were** fined heavily **and **villages were torched**. The British deemed the Indian National Congress to be an** illegal organisation**.
 
• The Quit India Movement, on the other hand, shifted the direction of negotiations with the British, eventually leading to** India's independence.​**

questions.question: WHO has partnered with Food and Beverage Alliance to achieve its target of eliminating which of the following from industrially produced global food supply by 2023?

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Trans fat,** also called the **worst form of fat **in food, is responsible for over** 5,00,000 deaths **globally from **coronary heart disease** each year.
 
• They not only **raise bad cholesterol (LDL)** levels but also **lower good cholesterol (HDL) levels**. This increases the risk of developing coronary heart disease and stroke. It also makes individuals prone to** a higher risk of developing type 2 diabetes.**
 
• The **World Health Organization (WHO)** has teamed up with the** International Food and Beverage Alliance (IFBA) **to achieve the **'REPLACE Strategy' **objective of eradicating **trans-fat** from the global food supply **by 2023.**
 
• By 2023, IFBA members have committed to not exceeding the** worldwide trans-fat industrial limit of 2 gramme per 100 g fat/oil** in their products.
 
• **REPLACE** is an abbreviation for **WHO’s six strategic actions**:
 
 
• Review (dietary sources of industrially-produced trans fats),
 
• Promote (replacement of industrially-produced trans fats with healthier fats,
 
• Legislate (enact regulatory actions to eliminate industrially-produced trans fats),
 
• Assess (trans fats content in the food supply),
 
• Create awareness (about negative health impact of trans fats) and
 
• Enforce (compliance with policies and regulations).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• This includes **rolls, buns, bagels, biscuits, and flour tortillas** (unless they are labelled "gluten-free").
 
• Gluten does** not include any vital nutrients.**
 
• **Celiac disease** causes an** immunological reaction** that is induced by gluten consumption. When they consume gluten-containing meals, their digestive tracts and other body components become inflamed and damaged.
 
 
 
• **Saturated fat:**
 
 
• Saturated fat is a** type of fat **found in foods. Along with trans fat, it is one of the** harmful fats.**
 
• At **room temperature,** these fats are usually **solid**.
 
• Saturated fat is found in foods such as **butter, palm and coconut oils, cheese, and red meat.**
 
• Saturated fat consumption can** enhance LDL cholesterol levels** in the blood. A **high LDL cholesterol level** in the blood raises your **risk of heart disease and stroke.**
 
 
 
• **Carotenoids:**
 
 
• Carotenoids are a **class of more than 750 **naturally occurring pigments synthesized by **plants, algae, and photosynthetic bacteria**.
 
• Many plants'** yellow, orange, and red colours **come from these brightly coloured molecules.
 
• The majority of the **40 to 50 carotenoids** contained in the human diet come from **fruits and vegetables.**
 
• Carotenoids are** antioxidants** that can help your **immune system** and protect you from disease.
 
• Vitamin A, which is required for growth, immune system function, and eye health, can be produced from **provitamin A carotenoids.**

questions.question: Which amendment in the Constitution of India deals with the abolition of Right to Property as a fundamental right?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**44th**__

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Articles 19 and 31** of the Constitution originally established the** right to property.**
 
• All citizens have the right to **acquire, keep, and dispose of property** under Article 19.
 
• "No individual shall be deprived of his property unless by authority of law," according to Article 31. It further stated that a person whose **property was taken** for** public reasons** would be** compensated. **
 
• The** 44th Amendment of 1978** **removed **the **right to property from the list of fundamental rights**. 
 
• A new provision,** Article 300-A**, was added to the constitution, which provided that "no person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law".
 
• Thus, if a legislator made a** law depriving a person of his property**, there would be **no obligation** on the part of the State to pay anything as compensation.
 
• Furthermore, the aggrieved person would also have** no right to move the court **under **Article 32 **due to the right to property no longer being a fundamental right.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **40th amendment:**

 
 
• The Constitution (40th Amendment) Act of **1976 empowered Parliament **to specify the **territorial waters, continental shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ), and marine zones of India **from time to time.
 
• It Included **64 more Central and state laws**, mostly relating to land reforms, in the **9th Schedule.**
 
 
 
• **42ⁿd amendment:**
 
 
• The Amendment established without a doubt **Parliament's primacy over the other branches of government**, gave **Directive Principles precedence over Fundamental Rights**, and **enumerated 10 Fundamental Duties** for the first time.
 
• It was implemented during a time of **national emergency**. Parliament passed it on **November 11, 1976**, and the President signed it on **December 18, 1976.**
 
• It also** limited the judiciary's power and jurisdiction, increased** the term of the Lok Sabha and Vidhan Sabha from** five to six years,** **authorised the use of Central armed forces **in any State to deal with law and order issues, bound the President to the advice of the Council of Ministers, and envisaged the establishment of **administrative tribunals **for government employees' service matters as well as other tribunals for economic offences.
 
• The Act also made it plain that** no constitutional amendment** could be **challenged in court.**
 
 
 
• **37th amendment:**

• According to **ohm’s law**, the **resistance R** is the** ratio of the voltage U **across a conductor and the** current I **flowing through it: **R = U / I.**
 
• Hence it follows: **1 Ω = 1 V/A. **
 
• The** ohm** is defined as an** electrical resistance** between two points of a conductor when a **constant potential difference of one volt,** applied to these points, produces in the conductor** a current of one ampere**, the conductor not being the seat of any electromotive force.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• The coulomb (C) is the **standard unit of electric charge** in the International System of Units (SI).
 
• It is a dimensionless quantity__, sharing this aspect with the** mole**.
 
• A **quantity of 1 C **is equal to approximately** 6.24 x 1018, or 6.24 quintillion.**
 
 
 
• **Seimens:**
 
 
• The siemens (S) is the **SI-derived unit of electric conductance and admittance**, also known as the** mho** (ohm spelled backward, **℧**); it is the **reciprocal of resistance in ohms** (Ω).
 
• The related property, **electrical conductivity**, is measured in units of **siemens per metre (S/m)**.

questions.question: The expression (tan A)/(1 space-space cot A) + (cot A)/(1 space-space tan A) can be written as:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Put a specific value for **angle A** where the expression is defined.

Let **A = 45°** is not possible as denominators become zero. Let **A = 30°**.

Expression = [tan 30° / (1 − cot 30°)] + [cot 30° / (1 − tan 30°)] = [(1/√3) / (1 − √3)] + [√3 / (1 − 1/√3)]

= [1 / (√3 − 3)] + [3 / (√3 − 1)] = 1 + 2/√3 + 1 = 1 + sec 30° cosec 30°.

**∴ The correct answer is 1 + sec A cosec A.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** (tan A)/(1 space-space cot A) + (cot A)/(1 space-space tan A)

**Formula Used:** tan A = sin A / cos A; cot A = cos A / sin A; a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e0e81c1e49b59329459f9a31e787008c87a7efdd2ac7b1bc9de4797ee74701f6.png] 

⇒ [(sin A / cos A) / (1 − cos A / sin A)] + [(cos A / sin A) / (1 − sin A / cos A)]

⇒ [sin² A / (cos A(sin A − cos A))] + [cos² A / (sin A(cos A − sin A))]

⇒ [sin² A / (cos A(sin A − cos A))] − [cos² A / (sin A(sin A − cos A))]

⇒ (sin³ A − cos³ A) / [sin A cos A (sin A − cos A)]

⇒ [(sin A − cos A)(sin² A + cos² A + sin A cos A)] / [sin A cos A (sin A − cos A)]

⇒ (1 + sin A cos A) / (sin A cos A)

⇒ (1 / sin A cos A) + (sin A cos A / sin A cos A) = sec A cosec A + 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1 + sec A cosec A.**

**__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Identities

sin² A + cos² A = 1 | 1 + tan² A = sec² A | 1 + cot² A = cosec² A.

Reciprocal Relations

cosec A = 1 / sin A | sec A = 1 / cos A | cot A = 1 / tan A.</p

questions.question: What are the three constituents of CPU in a computer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Control unit, ALU, memory.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• A **central processing unit (CPU)**, also called a central processor, main processor, or just processor, is the **electronic circuitry **that executes instructions comprising a computer program. The CPU performs basic **arithmetic, logic, controlling, and input/output (I/O) operations **specified by the instructions in the program.
 
• The three constituents of CPU in a computer are** the Control unit, ALU, and memory.**
 
• The **arithmetic and logical unit (ALU)** is a component that performs **arithmetic and logic operations** in all computers.
 
 
• The ALU is used to perform operations such as **addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, number comparison, and Boolean operations.**
 
• It does not deal with** instruction sequencing** or **memory directly.**
 
• A **smaller ALU **will produce** faster results** but **not always accurate** results, whereas a** larger one** will produce **slower but more accurate** results.
 
• ALU is like a** bridge** between the computer’s **primary memory and the secondary memory.** All the data and instructions that are exchanged between the primary and secondary memory pass through the Arithmetic and Logic Unit ( ALU ).
 
 
 
• The **Control Unit **reads the instructions that are stored in its memory and **send out electrical signals **to each component of the computer, telling them what to do with the data they've been given.
 
 
• Control Unit ( CU ) controls the** functioning of other hardware components **of the CPU like ALU and Registers,.
 
 
 
• A **memory or storage unit** in a computer is an **electronic device** that **stores data, programs, and other information.**
 
 
• The **two main types** of memory are **RAM and Hard Drive**. RAM stands for **Random Access Memory.**
 
• It is a **volatile type of storage** because it requires power to maintain its contents.
 
• It is mostly used for **temporarily storing data **while the computer is on.
 
• The **Hard Drive** is **non-volatile**, meaning it **retains stored **data even when power isn’t applied to it.
 
• It can be used to** store large amounts of data permanently,** so it is important for you to back up your files regularly.

questions.question: When a bicycle manufacturer reduced the selling price of a bicycle by 50%, the number of bicycles sold radically increased by 700%. Initially, the manufacturer was getting a profit of 140%. What is the new profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let initial **Cost Price (CP)** = 100. Since **initial profit** is 140%, initial **Selling Price (SP₁)** = 240.

New **Selling Price (SP₂)** = 50% of 240 = 120.

New **Profit** = SP₂ − CP = 120 − 100 = 20.

New **Profit %** = (20 ÷ 100) × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c837ddea20ac27e7aba92c0afeab3de3e0f61aaef1a1987cdc28ded26d951b45.png] 

**Given:** Initial Profit = 140%. SP reduction = 50%.

⇒ Let **CP** = 100 units.

⇒ Initial **SP** = CP + Profit = 100 + 140 = 240 units.

⇒ New **SP** = 240 × (100 − 50)/100 = 240 × 0.5 = 120 units.

⇒ New **Profit** = New SP − CP = 120 − 100 = 20 units.

⇒ New **Profit Percentage** = (New Profit ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ New **Profit Percentage** = (20 ÷ 100) × 100 = 20%.

**Note:** The 700% increase in sales affects **total revenue** and **total profit**, but the **profit percentage per unit** remains dependent only on the per-unit CP and SP.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit Percentage Formula

Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100. It is always calculated on the **Cost Price** unless stated otherwise.

Per Unit vs. Total Profit

Profit percentage per unit is independent of the **volume of sales**. Volume only affects the **absolute total profit** (Total Profit = Profit per unit × Number of units sold).

Effect of SP reduction

When SP is reduced by x%, the new SP = Original SP × (100 − x)/100.</p

questions.question: A works twice as fast as B. If both of them together can finish a job in 12 days, then how many days will B take to finish the job alone?

A works twice as fast as B. 

If both of them together can finish a job in 12 days

**Concept used:**

If a person can complete work alone in x days, then the efficiency (part of the work completed in one day) = 1/x

**Calculation:**

Let B's 1 day's work be x

Then A's 1 day's work = 2x

A and B's 1 day's work = 1/12

x + 2x = 1/12

⇒ 3x = 1/12

⇒ x = 1/36

So, B will take 36 days if he works alone

**∴ B will take 36 days to finish the job alone**
